subject: design/workbench-ui-v1
statement: One session per **working tree** (the statefile's home) — sibling worktrees of one repository run independent sessions over their own corpus states: launch mints a crypto-random secret, binds an ephemeral loopback port, writes the statefile into the render-scratch directory, and opens the browser at the secret URL. A second launch finds the statefile, probes liveness (pid + a guarded ping), and refuses with the named quadruple while the first lives (PRD UB-4) — a dead statefile is replaced, never trusted (acting on absence needs the liveness probe, AP-12/AP-17). The process exits on terminal end (SIGINT/SIGTERM), and auto-exits after a generous idle window with a named log line, so an abandoned session costs nothing (AP-19; default rides in the shape; revisit on usage evidence, Q1). Bind failure refuses the same way — no half-served state (UB-4). Exit removes the statefile; scratch pages are regenerable and may remain.
